## Accumulate and combine one stage (`user_stage_forcings`) {#sec-ch01-stage}

### Summary

One Runge-Kutta stage of a block is a fixed sequence. The hydro operator returns an increment, the scalar operator
returns its own, and user callbacks may add theirs. The integrator then combines the increments with the step-start
state. This section follows that sequence inside `advance_local` and writes out the three small identities the
combination and the tracer transfer rest on, because later chapters cite them.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Combine a stage (@eq-ch01-stage-combine, @eq-ch01-stage-weight); carry tracers (@eq-ch01-stage-dry).

**Data.** In: `hydro_u`, `scalar_s`, the stage weights, any user increments. Out: the combined interior state.

**Placement.** Once per RK stage, inside the block's advance, between the exchange and the physical fills.

**Activation.** User increments only with callbacks installed (`user_stage_forcings`); the stages are pyharp's.

**Guarantee / limits.** The combine is an affine recurrence in the weights, exact in arithmetic; no spatial order.

**Evidence.** `test_user_output.<b>` (rtol = atol = $10^{-12}$), `test_jit_user_forcing_python`; see the Tests layer.
:::
Local symbols: $J^{\mathrm{d}}_{i+1/2}$ is the already time-integrated implicit dry-air transfer through a face
[$\mathrm{kg}$], positive toward increasing $x_1$; $J^{\mathrm{tr}}_{n,i+1/2}$ is its upwind passive-tracer
transfer [$\mathrm{kg}$]. Here $n$ labels a passive tracer and $r_n$ is its ratio per unit dry mass.
Superscripts $\mathrm{carry}$ and $\mathrm{source}$ mark the selected carry ratio and a source increment.
These transfer symbols are defined locally above.

### Derivation

The fields in this section are cell averages. The conserved vector $\mathbf U$[^rg-879841a906d0] holds densities, momentum
densities and the energy density with the units of appendix A, and $\Delta t$ is the step [s].

Write $\Delta\mathbf U$ for the supplied stage increment, in the units of the corresponding conserved
component. The source comment states the combine as an in-place affine recurrence with the weights
$w_0^{(s)}, w_1^{(s)}, w_2^{(s)}$ of stage $s$:

$$
\mathbf U \leftarrow w_0^{(s)}\mathbf U^n + w_1^{(s)}\mathbf U + w_2^{(s)}\Delta\mathbf U.
$$ {#eq-ch01-stage-combine}

@eq-ch01-stage-combine is the recurrence stated in the comment beside `cw` in
{{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}}. The increment here includes whichever explicit and
implicit operations were selected, not only the explicit increment $\Delta\mathbf U^{(0)}$[^rg-e6248a941ab9] of appendix A.

Consider a fixed supplied increment in stage $s$, holding the later increments fixed. It enters the combination
with the coefficient $w_2^{(s)}$. The next combine multiplies this contribution by $w_1^{(s+1)}$, and the saved
step-start state contributes no copy of it. Repeating the substitution through each later stage gives the
final coefficient

$$
w_2^{(s)}\prod_{s'>s}w_1^{(s')}.
$$ {#eq-ch01-stage-weight}

@eq-ch01-stage-weight is the coefficient `cw` that {{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}}
accumulates for the gravity-work bookkeeping of @sec-ch06-fixer; the product runs over the remaining stages and
an empty product is one. The identity is exact for the bookkeeping of supplied increments; it is not a
linearization of their state dependence. The combine itself is the call `pintg->forward` in
{{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::advance_local >}}; the weights are pyharp's, so this chapter does
not assert their values from a snapy call site. Check `[C1]` expands a generic three-stage affine recurrence
symbolically [check `src/snapy_report/ch01/checks/stage_check.py`, output `stage_check.out`].

The tracer transfer and its dry-source complement are derived in @sec-ch10-tracer; this section keeps the call
interface, the three identities the code evaluates and the donor cap. Before the cap, the transfer of tracer $n$
through an $x_1$ face is the clamped dry transfer $J^{\mathrm{d}}$ of the implicit mass-correction buffer times the
ratio of the donor cell,

$$
J^{\mathrm{tr}}_{n,i+1/2} = J^{\mathrm{d}}_{i+1/2}
\begin{cases}
r_{n,i}, & J^{\mathrm{d}}_{i+1/2}>0,\\
r_{n,i+1}, & J^{\mathrm{d}}_{i+1/2}\le 0,
\end{cases}
$$ {#eq-ch01-stage-upwind}

the upwind tensor `P` of {{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::advance_local >}}. Each transfer is then
capped by what its donor holds, the `donor_cap` sweep ({{< code src/implicit/implicit_dispatch.cpp donor_cap_cpu >}},
{{< code src/implicit/implicit_dispatch.cu donor_cap_cuda >}}). Let $H_{n,i}$ [kg] be the tracer mass cell $i$[^rg-3f39479eeb50] holds
after the stage's explicit update, $V_i(\rho_{\mathrm d}r_n)_i$ with a negative value counted as zero. Up one column, from
the lowest interior cell $i_l$:

1. *Start.* $A_{i_l}=H_{n,i_l}$, what the lowest cell can give.
2. *Clamp the face above cell $i$.* $J^{\mathrm{tr}}_{n,i+1/2}\leftarrow\min\big(\max(J^{\mathrm{tr}}_{n,i+1/2},-H_{n,i+1}),\,A_i\big)$:
   an upward transfer takes at most $A_i$, a downward one at most what cell $i+1$ holds.
3. *Carry up.* $A_{i+1}=H_{n,i+1}+J^{\mathrm{tr}}_{n,i+1/2}$: what cell $i+1$ holds plus what entered it from below,
   never negative because of step 2.
4. *No cell goes negative.* Cell $i$ ends with $H_{n,i}+J^{\mathrm{tr}}_{n,i-1/2}-J^{\mathrm{tr}}_{n,i+1/2}=A_i-J^{\mathrm{tr}}_{n,i+1/2}$.
   An upward $J^{\mathrm{tr}}_{n,i+1/2}$ is at most $A_i$, and a downward one adds mass, so the result is $\ge0$.
5. *Conservation.* Each face value is used by both of its cells, so the column total is unchanged.
6. *A uniform ratio is untouched.* The VIC[^rg-828441330efe] clamps the dry transfer by the same rule (@sec-ch07-vic-redistribute).
   With one ratio $r_n$ everywhere, $J^{\mathrm{tr}}=r_nJ^{\mathrm{d}}$ and $H_n=r_nH_{\mathrm d}$, so every tracer bound is
   $r_n$ times a dry bound the dry transfer already meets, and the cap does not bind (the `through` test measures it).

The CPU first tests every face against $H_{n,i}$ plus the unclamped inflow and runs the sweep only if one binds,
which gives the same result; CUDA[^rg-28386113293d] runs the sweep in one thread per column with no host read. Check `[C4]` ports the
sweep. The increment of a cell is the net capped transfer over its volume $V_i$[^rg-902e93eb3066] [$\mathrm{m^3}$],

$$
\Delta\rho_{n,i} = \frac{J^{\mathrm{tr}}_{n,i-1/2}-J^{\mathrm{tr}}_{n,i+1/2}}{V_i},
$$ {#eq-ch01-stage-transfer}

the `P - P_above` update of the same function; and a supplied dry-mass source carries the tracers at the
selected carry ratio $r^{\mathrm{carry}}_n$,

$$
\Delta\rho^{\mathrm{source}}_n = r^{\mathrm{carry}}_n\,\Delta\rho^{\mathrm{source}}_{\mathrm{d}},
$$ {#eq-ch01-stage-dry}

the closure `carry_dry_source` of {{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::advance_local >}}. Checks
`[C2]` and `[C3]` exercise the two identities on a port, with the committed output `stage_check.out`; they
import no snapy.

### Numerical method

`MeshBlockImpl::advance_local` ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::advance_local >}}) first publishes the
stage to the hydro module, and on stage zero saves the step-start state and, when the gravity-work fixer is on,
resets its bookkeeping. With `implicit_radial`[^rg-4ddc775769de] diffusion on the cubed sphere it first takes a radial conduction
half step and refills the ghosts, and takes the second half step after the last stage's average
(@sec-ch09-csdiffusion). The
hydro call (@sec-ch01-hydro) returns a time-integrated increment; the scalar call (@sec-ch01-scalar) then uses the
hydro dry-mass flux and the implicit dry transfer. Native dry sources carry the tracers before the callbacks; user dry
sources carry them after all callbacks, from the saved pre-callback scalar increment. A callback result may contain
only `hydro_du` and `scalar_ds`, with matching shapes. The integrator combines the stage, the solid cells are refilled
(@sec-ch11-solids). The last stage runs the saturation adjustment on the interior cells when a thermodynamics module
and a nonempty reaction list exist (@sec-ch10-satadj). The gravity-work fixer runs on the last stage when it is on and
not deferred to the mesh (@sec-ch06-fixer). The physical ghosts are filled last (@sec-ch11-timing). This map asserts
algebraic identities, not an observed convergence order.

@fig-ch01-stage-flow shows the call sequence.

```{python}
#| label: fig-ch01-stage-flow
#| fig-cap: "Accumulate and combine one stage. Labelled green boxes name operations or owners; black arrows show the reading sequence, not a timing measurement."
#| fig-alt: "Sequence: publish stage / save; hydro increment; scalar / dry carry; user increments; RK / limiter / solids; last-stage adjustment / BC."
#| echo: false
from snapy_report.ch01.figures.fig_stage_flow import make_fig
make_fig()
```

**Why the combine is exact up to a bounded round-off.** Fix one cell and one row. The combine evaluates
$w_0\mathbf U^n + w_1\mathbf U + w_2\Delta\mathbf U$ with three products and two sums, five roundings in all, each
with relative error at most $\delta_{\mathrm{mach}} = 2^{-53}$. Dropping products of two rounding errors, the computed
value differs from the exact one by at most
$5\,\delta_{\mathrm{mach}}\,(|w_0\mathbf U^n| + |w_1\mathbf U| + |w_2\Delta\mathbf U|)$; the recurrence of
@eq-ch01-stage-weight inherits one such bound per stage. The transfer update of @eq-ch01-stage-transfer is three
operations per cell ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::advance_local >}}). They are the product $r_n M$
that forms each face transfer `P`, the subtraction `P - P_above`, and the division by the cell volume. Each product
rounds once, so the two transfers carry an absolute error of at most
$\delta_{\mathrm{mach}}(|J^{\mathrm{tr}}_{n,i-1/2}| + |J^{\mathrm{tr}}_{n,i+1/2}|)$ into the difference. The
subtraction itself is exact only when the two transfers have the same sign and lie within a factor of two of each
other. Otherwise it rounds once more, by at most $\delta_{\mathrm{mach}}$ of the difference. The division adds one
rounding of the result. When the two transfers nearly cancel, the product errors are not small relative to the result.
A capped transfer is a bound instead of the product: $A_i$ is one addition, one rounding, and the clamps themselves
are exact.

: Implementation anchors for one stage. {#tbl-ch01-stage-code}

1. Publish the stage and save the step-start state: `advance_local`
   ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::advance_local >}}).
2. Take the hydro and scalar increments, carry the tracers with the dry transfer (`mass_corr`) and the dry
   sources (`carry_dry_source`), apply the user callbacks ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::advance_local >}}).
3. Combine with `pintg`, refill solids, adjust saturation and run the fixer on the last stage, fill the
   physical ghosts ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::advance_local >}}).
4. The weight of a stage's increment in the step, `cw` ({{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}}).

**How to use it.** User increments are installed as scripted modules, one file per callback, in list order:

```cpp
mesh->set_user_stage_forcings({"heating.pt", "drag.pt"});
```

Each module receives the stage inputs, $\Delta t$ and the stage index, and returns a dictionary. It may contain
only `hydro_du` and `scalar_ds`, with the shapes of `hydro_u` and `scalar_s`. Any other key or shape is
refused ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::advance_local >}}). The weight of a stage's increment in
the step, @eq-ch01-stage-weight, is accumulated in these lines of `HydroImpl::forward`
({{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}}):

```cpp
// weight of this stage's du in the step's update u0 -> u1 (stage s:
// u <- w0 u0 + w1 u + w2 du): w2_s * prod_{t > s} w1_t (rk3: 1/6 1/6 2/3)
double cw = 1.;
auto const& st = pmb->pintg->stages;
if (rk_stage >= 0 && rk_stage < static_cast<int>(st.size())) {
  cw = st[rk_stage].wght2();
  for (int t = rk_stage + 1; t < static_cast<int>(st.size()); ++t)
    cw *= st[t].wght1();
}
```

The comment is @eq-ch01-stage-combine, the two assignments are the two factors of @eq-ch01-stage-weight.

: Source assertions for the stage. {#tbl-ch01-stage-tests}

The assertions are {{< code tests/test_user_output.cpp UserForcing.scripted_stage_forcings_add_tendencies_in_list_order >}},
{{< code tests/test_user_output.cpp UserForcing.scripted_module_is_shared_across_parallel_blocks >}},
{{< code tests/test_user_output.cpp UserForcing.scripted_stage_forcing_rejects_unsupported_keys >}} and
`main` of {{< code tests/test_jit_user_forcing.py main >}}.

The check is symbolic and numeric, with no snapy import.[^ch01-stage-run] `[C1]`: the supplied-stage
coefficients of a generic three-stage recurrence equal @eq-ch01-stage-weight, residuals 0. `[C2]`: the
upwind transfer telescopes over closed and open ends with residual 0 against a tolerance of
$1.4\times10^{-14}$. `[C3]`: the dry-source carry matches @eq-ch01-stage-dry on both branches, symbolic residual 0. `[C4]`: on
2000 random columns of 12 cells, all of which the cap binds, no cell ends below zero, the column changes by at most
$4.34\times10^{-16}$ relative, the CPU pre-test gives the sweep's result exactly, and a uniform ratio through a dry
transfer that obeys the same cap moves by at most $3.13\times10^{-16}$ relative.

The ctests run on CPU, one rank; `test_user_output.<b>` also runs the parallel-block case in one process. The two
donor-cap tests passed at the pin.[^ch01-stage-cap] `donor` printed a minimum tracer density of $0$ and a total
change of $2.22\times10^{-16}$; `through` a ratio change of $5.55\times10^{-16}$ with $1.433$ cell masses moved through a
cell; the upper-bound case a minimum of $0$. The callback tests have not been run for this report at the pin:
**pending a pinned ctest run**.

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
The stage algebra proves neither positivity after arbitrary user increments nor accuracy after nonlinear
limiting or phase adjustment. The donor cap keeps the implicit tracer transfer from overdrawing a donor; where it
binds, the tracer no longer moves with the ratio of the dry transfer, so a non-uniform ratio is changed there
(first order, donor-limited). Switch combinations remain subject to @sec-ch12-matrix; no new CPU, CUDA or
multi-rank snapy run is claimed.
:::
